title: Twenty-five named prophets
hookLine: the Qur'an names twenty-five prophets, from Adam to Muhammad ﷺ

lines: NOW: THE WHOLE BOOK, BY THEME.
cards: Since the start of this year, the path has walked the Qur'an surah by surah, from the Opening to the edge of its last part.
Now it steps back, holds the book up like a map, and traces the roads that run all the way through it. The first road is people.

Open the book and, again and again, someone is there: a man building an ark, a boy in a well, a father on a mountain with his son. Count the prophets the Qur'an names, by the usual reckoning, and you get twenty-five.

teach.b: The word is nabi, a prophet.
Arabic lexicons connect it to naba', news: a nabi is one who receives news from Allah and passes it on. Some link it to a root meaning to be raised up. Beside it stands rasul, a messenger.
One explanation scholars give: every messenger is a prophet, but not every prophet was sent with a new message or law.
Here are the twenty-five names. Adam. Idris.
And Muhammad ﷺ, called the seal of the prophets in surah thirty-three. Eighteen of them appear in one passage of al-An'am, one name after another.

Some will sound familiar from the Bible: Noah, Abraham, Moses, David, John, Jesus. Hud and Salih, sent to the Arabian peoples of 'Ad and Thamud, have no counterpart there. And the list isn't the whole family.

The Qur'an says plainly that some messengers' stories it has told, and some it has not. A report in Musnad Ahmad puts the number of prophets in the tens of thousands, though scholars debate its chain.
The Qur'an also tells believers to say: we make no distinction between any of His messengers.
And a hadith in al-Bukhari gives the picture behind today's line: the prophets are brothers with different mothers and one religion. Different times, different peoples, one family.

how: The twenty-five prophets named in the Qur'an are taught as a list in Islamic schooling, and Muslims add "peace be upon him" (alayhi as-salam) after each prophet's name.

games.q: a friend asks: how many prophets were there? what does the Qur'an itself say?
o: some it has told of, and some it has not.
games.why: twenty-five are named, but the Qur'an says plainly that others were sent whose stories it doesn't tell.

practice: Starting with Adam, say each prophet's name you can remember, quietly or in your head, one per breath, without worrying about the order or the gaps.

When you get stuck, pause on the last name and recall one thing about him: an ark, a well, a staff, a whale. Muslims customarily add peace be upon him after each name; if that's your practice, add it.

wordCard.voice: Nabi. A prophet, one who brings news from Allah. Twenty-five are named in the Qur'an, from Adam to Muhammad ﷺ, and more are left unnamed. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a prophet. lexicons link it to naba', news.

carryVoice: Your line: they are one family. Twenty-five named, and many more untold. Day six hundred sixty-four, done.
